rationale: The workflow is a Gradle/Android build-and-test triggered on push to develop. It already caches Gradle via setup-java cache: gradle, so adding a separate actions/cache for ~/.gradle/caches (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) is contraindicated because an equivalent cache already exists. There is no matrix, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply, and there are no scheduled runs or measured duration history for the schedule/timeout patterns. The applicable reviewed optimization is P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: runs on the same branch represent the same workflow and a newer push supersedes an older check; this is build/test rather than release/deployment, and scoping the concurrency group by workflow+ref keeps branches isolated. Adding concurrency with cancel-in-progress cancels superseded in-progress runs while the latest run still completes fully, preserving every build/test/coverage/upload step and required-check coverage. No permissions, secrets, publishing/deployment, or new network access are introduced.
